clue.text: Pollock and other fish numbers returning

parts.note: a jack is a young pike, a fish other than the pollock of the surface

indicators.note: returning says the abbreviation for numbers is read backwards

explanation.surface: A fishmonger lists pollock alongside other fish, with their numbers coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pollock' looks like the fish, but it is the painter. 'returning' turns NOS into SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson Pollock was the American abstract painter, so his first name stands for the surname clue word.

clue.text: Legless man, one goes into pub to participate

indicators.note: in a down clue the leg is the bottom, so the man's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Joe is a man's name

indicators.note: goes into says the letter for one is placed within the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drunken man staggers into a pub to join the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' is British slang for very drunk, but here it docks the foot of JOE.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in is to take part in an activity with others.

clue.text: Badger picks up virus No 5 within city limits

indicators.note: within says the virus and numeral sit inside the city's limits
limits means only the first and last letters of city are used

parts.note: HIV is a virus
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A badger in a town catches a virus, number five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' is the verb, to nag; 'limits' gives CY from city.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester or nag them repeatedly, as is to chivvy.

clue.text: Season and turn Chinese food

parts.note: spring is a season
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A cook seasons and turns a dish in the wok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a cooking verb but is the time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp fried pancake filled with vegetables is a staple of Chinese takeaways.

clue.text: Clouds rising from Maghrib mines

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Clouds billow up from mines in North Africa's Maghrib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' in a down clue reads upwards; the Maghrib is north-west Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi are rain clouds, plural of nimbus.

clue.text: Actor producing a cliche in a state

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the name of the state

parts.note: Maine is a state of the USA

indicators.note: producing hints that the letters of a cliche are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: An actor trots out a hackneyed line while in an agitated state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is the anagram signal, and 'in' places the shuffled letters inside MAINE just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Londoner who starred in Alfie and Zulu is one of Britain's best-known film performers.

clue.text: Film work on a second job

definitions.meaning: the 2016 Oscar-winning picture directed by Barry Jenkins
to take extra work, often secretly, beyond one's main employment

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means holding an extra job on the side; the title is a Best Picture winner.

clue.text: Allegedly, media mogul's a hood

indicators.note: allegedly says this is only how it is said, a sound-alike of the mogul's name

parts.note: Simon Cowell is a TV and music mogul

explanation.surface: A rumour claims a media tycoon is a gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hood' suggests a hoodlum, but it is the garment; Simon Cowell is the X Factor judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a large loose hood, as on a monk's habit.

clue.text: Revised bible held by a theologian's all made up

indicators.note: held by says the rearranged letters sit inside the theologian's letters

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

indicators.note: revised suggests a new version, so the letters of bible are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theologian claims a revised Bible is pure invention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' is the anagram signal; 'held by' puts the result inside a Doctor of Divinity's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libbed means improvised, spoken without preparation or script.

clue.text: Armageddon might take a while?

definitions.meaning: the end of the world, the final conflict
read as a verb phrase, something that will go on, endure, for days

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading uses 'last' as the verb to endure and 'days' as the duration.
explanation.definitionFit: The end times before judgment are the final period of the world; something enduring for days takes a while.

clue.text: Since I wear layers, it's more cold

indicators.note: layers suggests alternating strata, so every other letter of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone explains they wear layers because it is getting colder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' picks the even letters of SINCE I WEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, meaning colder, frostier.

clue.text: Promenades that are out of this world

definitions.text: Promenades that are out of this world

parts.words: Promenades that are out of this world
parts.note: strolls that are literally off this planet, on the lunar surface; also the gliding dance step of the theme's singer

explanation.surface: Seaside walks so lovely they seem heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of this world' means wonderful on the surface but literally on the Moon here.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts strolling on the lunar surface take walks beyond Earth, a literal reading of the idiom.

clue.text: Cable binds black line after home's impossible to conquer

indicators.note: after places the rest following the word for home

parts.note: at home means in, so home gives IN

indicators.note: binds means the politician's first name wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Sir Vince Cable is a UK Liberal Democrat politician
B is the abbreviation for black and L for line; the extra I needed here comes from no clue word, a slip the setter admitted on the fifteensquared blog

explanation.surface: A cable wrapped round a black line makes a house impregnable.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's slip: no clue word supplies the I that 'binds' needs inside VINCE alongside B and L; Qaos admitted the error in the fifteensquared comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbeatable cannot be overcome or defeated by any opponent.

clue.text: Nothing evil in short book?

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
bad means evil

explanation.surface: A brief book with nothing wicked in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Obadiah is the shortest book of the Old Testament, and Obad is its standard abbreviation, so 'short' works twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for the prophet Obadiah's book is a shortened biblical book name.

clue.text: Prepare clues for Everyman to begin with, Sunday lights up

indicators.note: prepare means the letters are made ready in a new arrangement
to begin with takes only the first letter of Everyman

explanation.surface: A setter readies clues for Sunday's Everyman puzzle, and it brightens things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the Observer's Sunday cryptic; 'Prepare' rearranges CLUES FOR E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fluorescing glows, giving off light when energised.

clue.text: Squeeze right into ship where hacks might be found

parts.note: to press is to squeeze

indicators.note: into says the letter for right goes inside the ship

parts.note: a galley is a type of ship

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cram right into a ship where journalists hang out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks' are journalists here, not horses or computer intrusions.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament's reporters' gallery is the seating reserved for journalists covering debates.

clue.text: Tailor cries over Trump becoming more untidy

indicators.note: over says the rearranged letters cover the word for trump
to tailor something is to alter it, so the letters of cries are rearranged

parts.note: to ruff is to trump in card games

explanation.surface: A tailor complains that Donald Trump is getting scruffier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' is the card-game verb, not the president; 'Tailor' rearranges cries to SCIER, which 'over' wraps round the trump word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruffier is the comparative of scruffy, shabby and unkempt.

clue.text: Remove dish to fridge

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or spoil, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Take the plate out and put it in the refrigerator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like a plate but is the verb to spoil, rearranging TO FRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose of or eliminate something is to take it away.

clue.text: Time after time, I shall get the queen in sensational film

indicators.note: after puts the hour abbreviation behind the single letter

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
I'll is a contraction of I shall
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Time and again, I'll get the queen into a gripping movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' looks like an idiom but gives two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is an exciting, suspenseful story or movie.

clue.text: Joy for old Benn is without end: people oust leader!

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: without end says the politician's first name loses its final letter

parts.note: Hilary Benn is a Labour politician, son of Tony Benn

indicators.note: oust leader says the word for people loses its first letter

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A political rallying cry: joy for a former MP, as the people throw out their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' trims HILARY to HILAR; 'oust leader' cuts NATION to ATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhilaration is a feeling of great elation and happiness.

clue.text: Boxer carries cold, firm cloth

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
Muhammad Ali was a boxer
CO, company, is a firm

explanation.surface: A boxer brings a cold, solid piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' is a noun here, a company, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain-woven cotton fabric.

clue.text: Feeling tired, Mole takes shelter

indicators.note: takes means the word for mole holds the word for shelter

parts.note: a mole is a spy
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: A drowsy mole burrows somewhere snug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' is a secret agent, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy describes someone drowsy and ready for bed.

clue.text: I career around, then collapse

indicators.note: around says the word for career wraps the letter I

parts.note: to career is to run headlong

explanation.surface: Someone rushes about madly and then falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is a verb, rushing, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is a state of downfall or collapse, as of an empire or a building.

clue.text: Unorthodox final position of Humpty Dumpty?

definitions.meaning: after his great fall the nursery-rhyme egg was no longer sitting on the wall but down from it

explanation.walkthrough: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall in the nursery rhyme and had a great fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means weird or unconventional, and literally describes something that has dropped down from a wall.

clue.text: Train tickets over 85% off per person

indicators.note: removing 85 percent of seven letters leaves about one, the first

parts.note: each means per person

explanation.surface: Rail tickets at a huge discount, priced per passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is the verb, to instruct, not the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct or school someone.

clue.text: Fuel stored in older vehicles

indicators.note: stored in says the letters are kept inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Fuel is kept in old cars.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is a British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel oil used in road vehicles, a type of fuel.

clue.text: Spoiled cat: "I loved the good life"

indicators.note: spoiled suggests the letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pampered cat declares that it adored the life of luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoiled' looks like a description of the pampered cat, but it rearranges CAT I LOVED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase, made famous by Fellini's film, means a life of luxury and pleasure.

clue.text: See 5
Always in favour of First Lady (Republican)

parts.note: for means in favour of
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Someone is forever backing a Republican president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's spouse, but it is the first woman of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever means for all time, at every moment, perpetually.

clue.text: Welcome tale from the past

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome
a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A friendly greeting and an anecdote about bygone times.
explanation.definitionFit: History is the record of bygone events, everything that happened before now.
